steps.text: Mix all canned beans with onion and bell peppers in a large bowl.
In a small saucepan, combine sugar, vinegar, oil, dill, rosemary, and basil. Season with salt and stir over medium heat without boiling until sugar dissolves.
Pour warm dressing over bean mixture. Cover and marinate for at least 2 hours in the refrigerator before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Super-Duper Bean Salad
raw_recipe.description: Made with five types of beans, this tasty marinated bean salad is loaded with fiber and plant-based protein. It's a healthy addition to any meal.
raw_recipe.name: Super-Duper Bean Salad

recipeInstructions.text: Mix all canned beans with onion and bell peppers in a large bowl.
In a small saucepan, combine sugar, vinegar, oil, dill, rosemary, and basil. Season with salt and stir over medium heat without boiling until sugar dissolves.
Pour warm dressing over bean mixture. Cover and marinate for at least 2 hours in the refrigerator before serving.

review.reviewBody: If you like bean salad then you will LOVE this one! The flavors blend nicely and guests ask for seconds and thirds! I added a little more sugar to bring the sweet/sour more into balance. The longer it marinates in the refrigerator, the better it is!

I followed the recipe exactly except I added a can of black beans (rinsed/drained), shredded carrots & dried cranberries. Also we found everyone liked it better served warm. I used a slotted spoon to remove the salad from the oil mixture after it marinated overnight & put in a clean dish. There was plenty of flavor left on the beans without dripping off the fork..This is a great dish!

This was very easy to make. I actually only had edamames, kidneys, white, and green beans on hand, so I tossed that in with some onions, ADDED celery, and the dressing on top tasted great! The dressing is really what made the salad, sweet with a little bit of tang. Just be careful with the dressing--Do NOT let it boil!! It is also good served warm.

OK ... I made a few changes, some out of necessity. Could not find canned wax beans, which led me to substitute frozen (steamed lightly) green beans and limas (never could find wax beans...). Added (canned) black beans. Omitted the peppers. Cut down on the sugar (by about a third). I found I had no white vinegar, so substituted white-wine vinegar. I kept the herbs essentially as directed, but wonder how fresh herbs might have changed/improved the final product..... This recipe is very forgiving. I am enjoying having it for luch at work all this week. Thanks, Jessica!

This was the first time I ever made a bean salad and it is so easy, quick and delicious. I used what I had in the house so I substituted a purple bell pepper for the green pepper and only used cans of garbanzo and kidney beans and used fresh yellow bean from the farmers market. I also used a greek salad herb mix in place of rosemary. Finally I used a small amount of red wine vingear in addition to the distilled white wine.
I substituted black beans for the wax beans, used Italian green beans, cut the sugar in half and added about 3/8 tsp. salt. Everyone loves it! A definite keeper!

This was so easy and super tasty. I didn't have the proper spices so threw in what I thought would work. Instead of rosemary & basil I used a little thyme and celery seed, along with dill and garlic powder. Also used a red and orange bell paper and much more sweet onion than was called for. I think that any spices you prefer would work, but definitely stick with the prescribed amount of vinegar, oil, and sugar. Be warned this recipe makes a large amount!

This is so easy to make, and so tasty! I add an extra can of wax beans and an extra can of green beans, and leave out the lima beans. Black beans are also good in this salad. I also add a can of sliced carrots for color. It's a wonderful dish for picnics, get-togethers or barbeques.

i usually don't like bean salad but i followed this recipe exactly and it was great. i did let the marinade cool a bit before pouring it over so the beans wouldn't get mushy. i sliced my vidalia onion into rings so us non onion eaters could easily pick them out but they definately add to the marinade flavor. i love the peppers in this! it adds a nice crunch. i used 1/2 teaspoon salt.

This recipe is very versatile. I don't care for wax beans so I leave them out. I sometimes add white kidney beans, dark red kidney beans and green peas. I always add a can of shoepeg corn. Sometimes, if I have it, I throw in a spoonful of diced pimento and some green olives. The marinade makes it delicious no matter what you add.

Liked it a lot. Made a couple of changes: beans: 1 (13oz) can black beans, 1 can garbanzo beans, 1 can "6 Bean Blend" (39oz altogether) plus I used a little more of the dried herbs. Went Fantastic. 2nd batch I figured I'd use fresh herbs--disaster. I chopped them way too coarse and got 'wood' in my salad. I thought about trying to save it by draining the bean mixture and straining the dressing to return to salad, but never got around to it. Will use dried for sure and maybe a little more sweet onion for zip. A keeper! :-)
Colorful, nice blend of flavors that, the longer it sits, is enhance. A definite keeper>

Recipe was very helpful! I adjusted it some by adding some different vegetables & seasoning/spices. I substituted lime beans for great northern beans. Added 1 can of sliced carrots, 1 can of white hominy. (didn't have lima or kidney) Added larger diced cucs (seeded), black & green olives, sliced fresh garlic, pickled okra & capers. For the "dressing" I used apple cider/white balsamic vinegars, celery & garlic salt & mustard seeds (because I had them). I also substituted agave syrup instead of granulated sugar. Can't wait to try it!!
So simple to make!!! Great flavors you won't be disappointed. Made it as written.

I added a can of black eyed peas and I doubled the amount of liquid. But after chilling the salad over night, the liquid on top got a little gelled. Not sure why. But I’ll make it again and follow the directions completely. It tasted okay and we ate it all!
DELICIOUS!!!!!!!!!
Absolute best bean salad I've ever had. I make it all the time.
Really good.

This salad is easy to put together. I used red wine vinegar in place of the white vinegar, olive oil in place of vegetable oil and black beans in place of the Lima beans. Next time I will use less sugar as it is a little sweet, otherwise I would have given it 5 stars. My husband loved it just as I prepared it and didn't think that it was to sweet.

I loved my grandma's bean salad but no one had her recipe. I found this and tried it. The only change I made was I omitted the lima beans and added black beans. It was fabulous. Great for a summer picnic since it has no mayo to worry about being in the sun. Definitely will make again.
